summary.one_liner: Twisted is an event-driven Python framework for building internet applications, covering networking protocols such as HTTP, SSH, IRC, SMTP, IMAP and DNS.
summary.what_it_does: Twisted is a Python event-based framework for internet applications. It includes modules for web (HTTP clients and servers, HTML templating, a WSGI server), SSHv2 and Telnet clients and servers with terminal emulators, IRC/XMPP and other IM protocols, IMAPv4/POP3/SMTP mail, NMEA GPS receivers, and DNS clients and servers. It also ships twisted.trial, a unit testing framework for Twisted-based code. The README says it supports multiple event loops (select, poll, epoll, kqueue, IOCP, and GUI loops such as GTK+, Qt and wxWidgets), and third-party reactors can be plugged in.
use_cases: write an HTTP or WSGI web server
create SSH or Telnet clients and servers
build IRC, XMPP or other chat bots
parse GPS NMEA data from receivers
how_to_run: tox -l  # list test environments (from source checkout)
tox -e nocov  # run the full test suite without coverage
env TWISTED_REACTOR=epoll tox -e alldeps-withcov-posix  # run tests under a specific reactor
tox -e lint  # run coding standard checks
tox -e mypy  # run MyPy type checks
notable: Covers many protocols (web, SSH, mail, IRC, DNS, GPS) in one framework
Pluggable event loop reactors: select, poll, epoll, kqueue, IOCP, GUI loops
Documentation hosted on Read the Docs with how-tos and API reference
caveats: Some test suite tests may fail without required subsystem dependencies, open firewall ports, or when run as root
Installing from source and running the full test suite relies on tox
